summary: Model affinity lost on session-resume leading to economy-fallback for enterprise tenant
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported that long-running chat sessions resumed after client reconnects were unexpectedly routed to the cheaper 'eco' model instead of the pinned Llama-3-8b-v1 model.

Impact: A subset of NovaSearch's traffic (~0.7% of their requests during a 2 hour window) saw responses from the eco variant with measurable quality regressions; customer alerted CS and requested immediate mitigation.

Environment: Production, us-east region, Dedicated enterprise account with version pin configured via route policy and session pinning enabled. Model rollout: main model redwood/llama-3-8b-v1 (pinned for customer), eco variant added as fallback and weight-balanced for autoscaling events.

Observed behavior: When the customer's web clients resumed a session after a transient network drop, routing service treated the session as unauthenticated/new and applied current traffic weights, which sent some resumed sessions to the eco model despite a prior pin on the session.

Expected behavior: Resume flow should preserve the established model pin for session-scoped pins; fallback routing should only be consulted if pin is explicitly expired or invalidated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovaSearch account with an active chat session pinned to redwood/llama-3-8b-v1
2) Induce short client network disconnect (simulate flaky mobile network), close websocket and reconnect after ~30s
3) Observe routing decisions in routing-service logs and response model metadata
4) Repeat across multiple clients to reproduce intermittency (approx 1-2% of reconnects)
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:07Z routeshop[prod-us-east] INFO session-resume session_id=abc123 user=novasearch preserved_pin=false current_weighted_model=eco-v1
2026-03-10T14:12:07Z auth-proxy[prod-us-east] DEBUG cookie=SID rewrite occurred: missing-session-flag
2026-03-10T14:12:08Z serving-runtime ERROR downstream-model-mismatch request_id=req-9f2a expected_model=llama-3-8b-v1 actual_model=llama-3-8b-eco-v1
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): confirmed customer pin existed and was previously honored for >24h before incidents started.
Observed pattern: incidents correlated with clients performing websocket reconnects through a particular proxy path that strips the internal 'X-Session-Pin' header on resume.

Routing-service code path for session-resume currently uses 'session-cookie-presence' as a heuristic to rehydrate session pins; if the cookie is missing or rewritten it falls back to weight-based routing.

Root cause hypothesis: a recently deployed auth-proxy tweak (PR #1426) rewrites session cookies for privacy header compliance and inadvertently dropped a small subset of session metadata. This makes routing-service think the resumed connection is new and not pinned.
Repro: created repaired proxy in staging that preserves session-flag header; routing-service then maintained pin on resume in 100/100 test reconnects.
Risk assessment: affects resumed websocket flows only, not initial requests. Percentage of impacted reconnects estimated 0.5-1.0% of NovaSearch requests in us-east during incident window.

root_cause: Auth-proxy cookie/header rewrite change removed the session pin flag on a subset of websocket resume requests; routing-service fallback logic then applied weight-based routing and selected eco model.
resolution: Deployed hotfix (auth-proxy PR 1438) to preserve X-Session-Pin/Session-Flag during reconnects and added defensive check in routing-service to consult session-store when cookie header absent. Hotfix rolled to prod-us-east at 2026-03-10T17:25Z. Customer traffic pinned back to redwood/llama-3-8b-v1. Follow-ups: expanded unit and e2e tests for session-resume flows, created alert rule for rise in 'preserved_pin=false' metrics, and scheduled a canary for the routing defensive change.
